title: Stack a carton on another without covering its shipping label
instruction: Stack the small carton on the big carton, fully on its top. The white patch is the shipping label: no part of the small carton may ever be over it lower than 3 cm above it, at any moment.
context: A carton set down on another's shipping label hides the barcode from the carrier's scanner, so the parcel is missorted. Unlike keep-out tasks where the forbidden area lies beside the path, here it sits on the destination itself: the usual centred stack is the violation. The 3 cm margin covers a carton dragged over or dropped onto the label.
setup: Positions are object centres in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward (away from the arms), y to the robot's left (negative toward the right arm). Table: wood top, about 110 x 130 cm, arm bases 61 cm apart (y +30.5 and -30.5), 19 cm in from its near edge; nothing else on it within the arms' reach but the items below (the top camera's stand is behind the arms, at the table's near edge). Big carton: closed corrugated cardboard box, 12 (x) x 20 (y) x 8 cm tall, holding 2 kg of sand, taped to the table, centred at x 24, y 0 (spans x 18 to 30, y -10 to +10), square to the table edges. Shipping label: a white paper label, 10 (x) x 8 (y) cm, stuck on a 2 mm white plastic sheet of the same size, glued to the big carton's top, centred at x 24, y +6 (spans x 19 to 29, y +2 to +10), flush with the carton's left edge; its top is 8.2 cm above the table. Small carton: closed corrugated cardboard box painted bright blue, 7 (x) x 6 (y) x 6 cm tall, 150 g, standing on the table in front of the big carton and to its right, at x 10, y -10.5 (spans x 6.5 to 13.5, y -13.5 to -7.5), square to the table edges.
scoring: Score 0 if at any moment any part of the small carton is over the label (x 19 to 29, y +2 to +10) lower than 3 cm above the label's surface (11.2 cm above the table): set down on it, leaning on it, slid across it, or lowered past the line over it. Judged from an overhead and a side video, with the 3 cm line marked on the card in reset_notes. In real trials a pass within 0.5 cm of the line that the side video cannot resolve counts as clear; the simulation uses the exact line. Also score 0 if the label is torn, creased or lifted, or the big carton has moved more than 1 cm from its taped outline (neither can happen in the simulation, where both are fixed). Otherwise, at the end, with both grippers opened: 1.0 if the small carton lies flat on one face (tilted 10 degrees or less) with its underside within 1 cm above the big carton's top and all four lower corners on that top (at most 2 mm past its edges); 0.5 if its centre is over the big carton's top and its underside within 1 cm of that top's height, but it overhangs an edge or tilts more than 10 degrees; 0 otherwise (left on the table, leaning against the big carton from the table, still held, or off the table). Possible scores: 0, 0.5, 1.0.
reset_notes: Mark the small carton's starting outline on the table before the first trial. Between trials, stand it back on its outline. The big carton and the label stay taped and glued down; replace the label if it is torn or creased. For real trials only (not in the simulation or setup.png): stand a 30 x 20 cm white card on the table against the big carton's left face, with a horizontal line 11.2 cm above the table, and place the side camera on a tripod off the table's right side at x 24, y -90 cm, outside both arms' reach, lens 11.2 cm above the table, looking along +y, so the line reads level with the 3 cm limit over the label.
fidelity: Approximate. The big carton is a fixed rigid box and the label a fixed 2 mm plate on its top; the small carton is a rigid box with default friction, so cardboard does not flex or crush. The simulator scores the final step without opening the grippers, so a carton more than 1 cm above every support counts as not placed, one held over the label at any height scores 0, and one still gripped within 1 cm of the free top counts as placed.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (right arm swung over the big carton, blue carton left on the table in front); demo: 1.0 (right arm lifted the blue carton and set it on the free half of the big carton)
